summary: This article explains how the Red Sea sits inside a slowly widening crack between the African and Arabian plates, and why its water is some of the saltiest and warmest on Earth.
introduce: Show the title “The Red Sea: Between Two Continents” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: having to do with the huge moving plates that make up Earth's crust
a long, deep crack where two plates of Earth's crust slowly split apart
a bowl-shaped dip in the land or sea floor where water can collect

challengeTerms.def: the branch of science that studies the huge plates of Earth's crust and how they move
the amount of salt dissolved in a body of water
the process by which a liquid changes into vapor, usually from heat

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that two continents are slowly pulling apart underneath the Red Sea? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how moving tectonic plates and a hot, dry climate together shape the Red Sea.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review tectonic, rift, and basin, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses tectonics, salinity, and evaporation to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
